feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: ELM's Hillslope Hydrology (HHM) mode can represent a discretized hillslope of connected columns with lateral saturated subsurface flow and column-to-column groundwater exchange, but explicit water 'travel times' (transit-time distributions) are NOT a native ELM diagnostic and require offline particle tracking or a coupled PFLOTRAN reactive-transport/age-tracer simulation.
answerable: Steady-state and transient lateral subsurface (saturated) flow convergence along a topographic flowpath using ELM hillslope columns ordered upland->stream
Groundwater exchange (lateral saturated flux) between adjacent hillslope-position columns via QDRAI_XS / lateral flow diagnostics
Water-table depth, saturated-zone storage, and drainage timing per hillslope position, from which effective residence/travel-time proxies can be estimated
Sensitivity of convergence and exchange to slope, column length, and soil texture along the transect
not_answerable: Direct hillslope-to-stream water travel-time (transit-time) distributions from ELM alone — ELM carries no age/tracer state; requires PFLOTRAN age tracer or offline Lagrangian particle tracking
Fully 3-D convergent-plan-form flow accumulation across a real 2-D DEM (ELM HHM uses a 1-D chain/branching representation, not full 3-D routing)
Any validation against streamflow or water-table observations (none available in this domain)

parsed.n_justification: A single representative Naches hillslope is discretized into 5 sequential columns spanning the hydrologic gradient (upland ridge -> upper backslope -> midslope -> footslope -> riparian/stream-adjacent). This is the minimum discretization that resolves downslope lateral-flow convergence and neighbor-to-neighbor groundwater exchange while keeping the ELM HHM chain tractable; more columns add resolution but not new process representation.
requires_capabilities: ELM Hillslope Hydrology (HHM) configuration with multi-column hillslope discretization and column connectivity (hillslope_pft/col topology, downhill flow ordering)
Lateral saturated subsurface flow between connected columns enabled (use_lateral_flow / hillslope hydrology namelist)
Surface-dataset generation with per-column hand-off of elevation, slope, aspect, and column length from a DEM along the flowpath
PFLOTRAN coupling (or offline Lagrangian particle tracking) with an age/tracer species to derive explicit hillslope-to-stream transit-time distributions
GSWP3/CRUNCEP or elevation-corrected reanalysis forcing for 1980-2018
assumptions: A single representative convergent hillslope near the Naches mainstem (~46.89N, 121.20W) is used as the archetype; results are typologically representative, not spatially exhaustive.
Slope/length attributes for each column are extracted from a 1/3-arcsec DEM (elevation range 352-1977 m); columns are ordered strictly downslope with column 5 as the stream-adjacent discharge node.
Soil textures grade from coarser sandy_loam on uplands to finer silty_clay_loam in the riparian zone, a common catena pattern; refine with SSURGO/POLARIS if available.
No streamflow or water-table observations exist for this HUC (per brief), so the experiment is diagnostic/mechanistic and unvalidated.
Travel-time estimates from ELM alone are effective proxies (storage/flux and water-table timing); quantitative transit-time distributions require the PFLOTRAN age-tracer capability listed above.
A multi-year spin-up (recycle 1980-2018 forcing) precedes the analysis period to equilibrate the saturated zone before interpreting convergence and exchange fluxes.
